MATERNAL SEPSIS: SCREEN, 1-HOUR BUNDLE, ESCALATE CHRISTUS St. Michael / OBHG · Texarkana
SYS-03 · With SYS-01, LND-04 · SMFM CS #67 (2023) · CMQCC Sepsis Toolkit (2020) · ACOG CO 712, PB 211 · All units, ED · Decision support only, not unit policy
18 October 2026
HOW TO READ THIS CHART: start at Step 0. Hexagons are questions; shaded rectangles are actions. Fever is not required. No single screening tool alone (SMFM); qSOFA missed half of maternal sepsis (sensitivity 50%) and SIRS over-calls in pregnancy (specificity 63%) (CMQCC).
SHADING KEY: WHITE = screen negative LIGHT GRAY = watch, notify MID GRAY = sepsis DARK GRAY = time zero, septic shock, ICU
STEP 0: SUSPECTED INFECTION
Pregnant, postpartum, or after abortion; any
unit including ED. Fever is not required
(SMFM). RN runs the screen.
STEP 1: CMQCC SCREEN: 2 OR MORE?
Temp <36 or ≥38 °C; HR >110 sustained 15 min; RR >24 sustained 15 min; WBC >15,000 or <4,000/mm
3
or >10% bands. Recheck an abnormal value with full VS and SpO2 in 15 min. MAP <65 with suspected
infection: sepsis protocol now.
NO
SCREEN NEGATIVE · WHITE
Keep screening through labor and until discharge; VS between contractions.
Infection still suspected (eg, CVA tenderness with low-grade temp; prolonged
ROM with maternal or fetal tachycardia): do Step 2 labs anyway (CMQCC).
YES
SCREEN POSITIVE = TIME ZERO · 1-HOUR BUNDLE
RN notifies the OBHG hospitalist and charge RN now; hospitalist to the
bedside. Within 1 h: lactate; blood cultures x2 before antibiotics if no delay;
broad-spectrum antibiotics by source (strips A1, A2); 1 to 2 L balanced
crystalloid if hypotension or hypoperfusion (strip B). Step 2 labs: CBC with
bands, PT/INR, PTT, CMP with bilirubin and creatinine. Foley with urometer;
SpO2; mental status.
STEP 2: ANY ORGAN INJURY? (CMQCC)
New ventilation need or PaO2/FiO2 <300; platelets <100 x 10
9
/L, INR >1.5, or
PTT >60 s; bilirubin >2 mg/dL; after fluids SBP <85, MAP <65, or SBP fall >40
mm Hg; creatinine ≥1.2 mg/dL, doubled, or urine <0.5 mL/kg/h x2 h; agitated,
confused, or unresponsive; lactate >2 mmol/L not in labor. One is enough.
NO
NO ORGAN INJURY · LIGHT GRAY
Still high risk: keep treating the infection, close supervision, reevaluate;
any new criterion = Step 2 YES. In labor with elevated lactate only: at
minimum close surveillance, consider more fluid, repeat lactate (lactate
rises in normal labor).
YES
STEP 3: SEPTIC SHOCK?
MAP <65 mm Hg sustained 15 min after fluid resuscitation (CMQCC), or a
vasopressor needed to keep MAP 65 with lactate >2 mmol/L after adequate
fluids (Sepsis-3, PB 211)?
NO
SEPSIS CONFIRMED · MID GRAY
Fluids per strip B, reassessing after each bolus; repeat lactate; close surveillance
and rapid response team per CSM; escalate as needed. Source control (Step 4).
Worse at any reassessment: back to Step 3.
YES
SEPTIC SHOCK · ICU NOW (SYS-01)
Norepinephrine first line (SMFM); initial target MAP 65, not studied in
pregnancy: individualize to perfusion (mentation, urine, lactate, fetal status).
Vasopressin second line; dobutamine for myocardial dysfunction.
Norepinephrine or epinephrine ≥0.25 mcg/kg/min for ≥4 h: hydrocortisone
200 mg/day (50 mg IV q6h). VTE prophylaxis; insulin if glucose >180 mg/dL.
Adult ICU accepts her; transfer only if stable, never past an available OR or
ICU.
STEP 4: FIND AND CONTROL THE SOURCE
Identify or exclude an anatomic source fast; emergency source control when
indicated (SMFM). Least invasive effective route (strip C).
STEP 5: STILL PREGNANT?
Stabilize her first; maternal resuscitation usually improves the FHR.
Strip D.
SURGERY OR TRANSFUSION NEEDED
OBHG hospitalist notifies the private attending. No routine call otherwise.
A1 · ANTIBIOTICS BY
SOURCE
IAI/chorio (LND-04 card; CO 712): ampicillin 2 g IV q6h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h (or 2 mg/kg, then 1.5 mg/kg q8h); add clindamycin 900 mg or metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h for cesarean. Endometritis
(CMQCC): clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h (or metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h) + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h + ampicillin 2 g IV q6h; or ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h. Pyelonephritis
(CMQCC): ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h or cefepime 2 g IV q12h; severe penicillin allergy: aztreonam 1 g IV q8h; MDRO risk: ertapenem 1 g IV q24h or meropenem 1 g IV q8h.
A2 · ANTIBIOTICS (CONT.)
Septic abortion or retained products (CMQCC): cefoxitin 2 g IV q6h or cefotetan 2 g IV q12h + doxycycline 100 mg PO or IV q12h; or clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h + gentamicin 3 to 5 mg/kg IV daily. Septic
abortion or periviable sepsis: alert house supervisor or CMO. Necrotizing wound (CMQCC): piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 g IV q8h extended infusion (or 4.5 g q6h) + vancomycin per protocol + clindamycin
900 mg IV q8h; GAS or clostridia: penicillin G 4 million U IV q4h + clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h. Non-necrotizing wound (CSM house regimen): PO amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID x 7 days; IV
ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h, OR piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h (confirm infusion schedule with CSM pharmacy). Unknown source or septic shock (CMQCC Table 9): piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 g IV
q8h extended (or 4.5 g q6h), or meropenem 1 g IV q8h if MDRO risk, plus vancomycin 15 to 20 mg/kg IV q8 to 12h (load 25 to 30 mg/kg if critically ill). Doses assume normal renal function.
B · FLUIDS AND
REASSESSMENT
Hypotension or suspected hypoperfusion: 1 to 2 L balanced crystalloid (LR, Plasma-Lyte) IV in the first 3 h (SMFM); septic shock may need a total of 30 mL/kg in the first 3 h: individualize. SMFM: 30 mL/kg
"may be overly aggressive in pregnancy" (lower oncotic pressure, more pulmonary edema): extra caution in preeclampsia, cardiac disease, or pulmonary edema risk; measured aliquots (SYS-01). No starches or
gelatin. Reassess after each bolus with dynamic measures (passive leg raise with uterine displacement, 250 to 500 mL bolus with cardiac output, POCUS); not fluid responsive or lungs wet: vasopressor.
Lactate: repeat if >2 mmol/L (CMQCC order set: at 3 h); CMS also treats lactate ≥4 as shock (CMQCC App A); read with caution in labor. MAP and temp q30 min until lactate <2; urine hourly (CMQCC).
C · SOURCE CONTROL
Uterine source (IAI, infected retained tissue, septic abortion): prompt delivery or evacuation regardless of GA (SMFM); IAI alone is not a cesarean indication (LND-04). Retained products: ultrasound, D&C. Septic
abortion or periviable sepsis: alert house supervisor or CMO. Wound: open and culture; deep or organ space: CT and ultrasound; necrotizing: early surgical debridement, hysterectomy if myometrial necrosis.
Pyelonephritis/obstruction: renal ultrasound antepartum, CT with contrast postpartum; drainable abscess: IR; obstructed infected kidney: urology decompresses (CSM). Pelvic abscess: ultrasound or CT; IR
drainage. Percutaneous over open surgery, except necrotizing infection (SMFM).
D · FETUS AND DELIVERY
Sepsis alone is not an immediate indication for delivery, except IAI (SMFM). Deliver for the usual obstetric indications; cesarean is usually reserved for obstetric indications after she is stabilized (CMQCC). Fetal
monitoring after maternal stabilization if viable; at the limit of viability, include her or her family's preferences. Septic abortion or periviable sepsis: alert house supervisor or CMO. Antenatal steroids are not
contraindicated. Strongly consider avoiding neuraxial in sepsis or shock; anesthesia decides (CMQCC).
E · NOTIFY AND ESCALATE
RN: positive screen to OBHG hospitalist and charge RN. Hospitalist: critical care or ICU (SYS-01), anesthesia, neonatology; MFM via the local MFM call schedule posted in the call lounge; ID or surgery as needed.
Private attending: only if surgery or transfusion is needed. Concern about the plan: charge RN, then nursing director, then OBHG Site Director. Septic abortion or periviable sepsis: alert house supervisor or CMO.
Doses to be checked against CSM pharmacy build. GA = gestational age; IAI = intraamniotic infection; MDRO = multidrug-resistant organism; POCUS = point-of-care ultrasound. Decision support only, not unit policy. Cite: SMFM
Consult Series #67, Maternal sepsis, Am J Obstet Gynecol 2023;229:B2-B19; CMQCC, Improving Diagnosis and Treatment of Maternal Sepsis (2020, errata 2022), Box 1, Tables 3, 5, 9, 10, 11; ACOG CO 712, Obstet Gynecol
2017;130:e95-e101; ACOG PB 211, Obstet Gynecol 2019;133:e303-19.
